name: update_status_from_inverted_byte
description: Reads a byte at a fixed offset from the base register, inverts it and rotates it one bit into a global. It then sets bit 6 of a second byte, writes 1 to a third location and sets the global to 8.

name: clear_bit6_of_register_block
description: Clears bit 6 of a byte at a fixed offset from the base register and then stores 8 in a global. The facts record an INTREQ touch, which fits acknowledging an interrupt request bit.

name: advance_counter_state_machine
description: Steps a global value through range checks: depending on the range it returns, adds or subtracts fixed increments, or resets the value, calls another routine and retries the same branch.

name: run_stage_dependent_draw_loop
description: Returns at once when the stage value is zero. For higher stages it picks a base offset from the stage and writes three words per pass in a five-pass loop with a fixed stride; for lower stages it calls another routine four times and advances the stage.

name: setup_blitter_copy_rows
description: Computes a start offset from the stage value and an input register, adjusts it by constants and writes the blitter masks, modulo, pointer, control and size registers. It then runs a five-pass loop that steps the pointers by a fixed stride.

name: repeat_routine_and_advance_global
description: Calls another routine and advances a global counter by two on each pass, repeating one more time than the count held in a register.

name: stub_no_decompiled_body
description: The decompiler produced no body for this routine, and the facts report five instructions reached through an absolute address. Its behaviour cannot be determined from the evidence.

name: stub_calls_one_routine
description: The decompiler produced no body for this eight-instruction routine, which calls one unnamed routine. Its behaviour cannot be determined from the evidence.

name: copy_indexed_table_rows
description: Increments a global, branches on its value to pick one of four table bases and calls a routine in each case. It then copies pairs of bytes from the lookup table into a destination at a fixed row stride; the bundle reports only one instruction for this address, so the body may be misdecoded data.

name: decode_mouse_port_direction
description: Reads the mouse port movement register and reduces its bit patterns to a small direction state held in a global.

name: split_value_into_decimal_digits
description: Converts a value to digits by repeatedly subtracting entries from a zero-terminated table of place values and storing each count as one byte. It is a number-to-digits conversion.

name: test_position_against_bounds_storing
description: Tests a value against ranges built from two words at a pointer, each widened by 100 and a fixed offset. It returns zero when the value falls inside a range and a non-zero flag otherwise, and it also stores several values through the stack and the second pointer register.

name: test_position_in_bounds_box
description: Tests a value against ranges built from two words at a pointer, each widened by 100 and a fixed offset. It returns zero on a hit and a non-zero flag otherwise, without the stack stores of its neighbour.

name: repeat_routine_until_both_zero
description: Calls another routine repeatedly and loops while either of its two returned values stays non-zero, stopping once both are zero.

name: reset_state_and_clear_block
description: Decrements a state value and, through several branches, calls other routines, stores a lookup record and clears a block of words in a loop. The facts list the COLOR00 colour register as touched, and the bundle cuts the decompiled body off partway, so the full sequence cannot be confirmed.

name: clear_then_enable_dma_interrupts
description: Writes constants to the DMA and interrupt control registers, starting with a DMA set mask and a clear-all mask for the interrupt enables. It calls another routine between the writes and then writes further enable masks.

name: enable_dma_and_interrupt_bits
description: Writes a DMA set mask to the DMA control register and a clear-all mask to the interrupt enable register. It calls two routines around a final set mask for the interrupt enables.

name: return_without_action
description: The body is a single return with no work, so calling it has no effect.

name: move_position_by_key_code
description: Adjusts two 16-bit values in a table entry selected by the key code. Each of four comparisons against a key code adds or subtracts one from one of the values, so it looks like a keyboard direction update.

name: repack_value_nibbles
description: Divides the value by 200 and folds the quotient into the high nibble, then transforms the low nibble and combines the two. The result is written back to the same global.

name: reset_sprite_pointers_if_flagged
description: When a flag bit is set, it writes a fixed constant eight times, matching the eight sprite pointer registers listed in the facts, then calls another routine and sets a global. Otherwise it only sets a global to a fixed value.

name: summarise_timed_out_routine
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code is available. The facts show 62 instructions that touch the COLOR00 colour register and the DMACON DMA control register, a file path string, and a series of small move and OR routines.

name: call_routine_over_nested_grid
description: Runs a nested loop of 26 outer passes and 28 inner passes, calling another routine once per inner pass. The loop itself does no other work in this code.

name: call_routine_twenty_eight_times
description: Calls another routine 28 times in a row using a byte counter. The facts say the start of this body lies in a gap that decodes as code, so it may be misread data.

name: call_routine_if_value_high
description: Compares a global against a threshold and, when it is at or above it, calls another routine 26 times. Otherwise it returns without work.

name: call_routine_twenty_six_times
description: Calls another routine 26 times in a row using a byte counter and does nothing else.

name: call_routine_then_return
description: Calls another routine and then performs a self-assignment to a global, which has no effect, before returning. Four unnamed routines call it.

name: place_template_object_in_grid
description: Computes a grid cell from two register values and tests bit flags in a bitmap and a byte map. It returns if the cell is blocked or already marked; otherwise it marks the cell, calls another routine and fills a 30-byte record with coordinates scaled by 16 plus offsets from a template table.

name: fill_object_record_from_template
description: Marks a map byte as occupied, calls another routine and then fills an object record from a template picked by a table lookup. Coordinates are scaled by 16 with offsets, and 30 bytes of template data are copied into the record.

name: initialise_tables_and_records
description: Sets a run of globals to zero and a few constants, fills two record tables with minus-one values and clears a bit in a byte region. It calls several routines and runs a five-pass loop that writes two constants and calls a routine each pass, so it is setup code whose wider purpose is not recoverable from this body.

name: release_list_head_node
description: Returns when the list head is a sentinel. Otherwise it takes the first node, decrements the stored count, and either resets the node's fields when the count reaches minus one or links the node back into the list with its status byte set.

name: release_alt_list_head_node
description: Uses the same release logic as its neighbour but links through the other pair of node fields. It returns early for an empty list and resets the node status fields when the count reaches minus one.

name: unlink_node_from_list
description: Records a node pointer in a slot and unlinks the node from a doubly linked list through its two link fields, joining its neighbours together. If the node has no neighbours it resets the list head to an empty marker.

name: advance_pseudo_random_state
description: Increments a 32-bit counter, mixes it with a stored value using exclusive-or and additions, rotates the state bits and stores the low word in a global. It is a pseudo-random number generator step.

name: set_column_bitplane_pointers
description: Computes a pointer offset from a stored position and fills four bitplane pointers spaced by a fixed plane stride. When the mode flag is zero it also writes a longword to seven rows and copies a six-entry pattern; otherwise it only stores the pointer values.

name: pack_position_and_flag_words
description: Builds two 16-bit words at an output pointer: one from the high byte of one input and the shifted low byte of another, and one from a combination of comparison flags against the inputs. The register inputs are returned unchanged.

name: copy_column_block_entries
description: Copies a column of longword data from a shared buffer into an output area at a fixed row stride and sets an active flag bit in one word of each block. Depending on a stored flag it writes two constants and zeroes the rest, or writes more blocks and calls other routines several times.

name: clip_record_to_visible_window
description: Chooses one of two table entries from a flag in the record, then computes a clipped vertical range from a position and a fixed window size. When the range is visible it fills the record with the clipped bounds and a stride-derived pointer, and it calls several other routines.

name: emit_clipped_span_records
description: Clips a horizontal span to a window edge and fills a record with a size and pointer derived from the span. It then writes four rows of entries spaced by a fixed plane stride and calls another routine when the span starts left of the window.

name: emit_span_record_rows
description: When the span width is non-zero, fills a record with a size and pointer and writes four rows of entries at a fixed plane stride. It does no clipping of its own.

name: emit_span_record_at_offset
description: Takes an offset from its caller and, when the span width is non-zero, fills a record and writes four rows of entries at a fixed plane stride. It calls one other routine for its pointer data.

name: program_blitter_span_rows
description: Computes a source pointer from a scaled offset and a stored record, then writes four rows at a fixed plane stride. The facts list the blitter address, modulo, control and size registers as touched, so it sets up the same blitter masks and sizes as the span emitters.

name: walk_record_list_decrementing_counts
description: Clears a head pointer that matches a sentinel and then walks a linked list through its next-link field. For each node it calls another routine and decrements a byte counter in the node when it is non-zero, and it calls the routine for the remaining nodes afterwards. The facts say this body starts in a gap that decodes as code, so it may be misread data.

name: call_routine_per_list_node
description: Walks a linked list through its next-link field and calls another routine for each node until it reaches the end marker. The facts say the body starts in a gap that decodes as code, so it may be misread data.

name: call_routine_per_table_entry
description: Walks a table in fixed 14-byte steps, calling another routine for each entry until it reaches a zero entry.

name: program_blitter_rows_from_record
description: Copies two words from a record into stored values, then writes the blitter masks, modulo, size and control words and programs four rows at a fixed plane stride from the record's pointer. The facts list the matching blitter registers as touched.

name: advance_entity_state_machine
description: Runs a multi-branch state update on a counter and an object record pointer. Depending on the state it resets counters, calls other routines, fills object records with computed coordinates and attributes, and then sets the next state. The decompiler output is heavily garbled, so only the overall shape is recoverable.

name: step_value_down_when_blocked
description: Sets a global to a fixed value when it is below a threshold. Otherwise it calls another routine and, if the result is zero, decrements the global by two and resets two other globals.

name: clamp_value_or_advance_step
description: Caps a global at a fixed threshold when it reaches it. Otherwise it calls another routine and, if the result is zero, adds two to the global and sets two other globals.

name: map_index_through_lookup_tables
description: Maps a small state index through one of several lookup tables and leaves the looked-up value in a global. Some branches call two other routines first, and out-of-range indexes return a fixed value.

name: poll_fire_button_port
description: Reads the CIA port register that carries the fire buttons and disk status, and updates a per-button state in a loop. It calls two other routines and picks a result from one of several tables.

name: countdown_linked_record_state
description: Calls another routine eight times, then decrements a per-record counter and, while the counter stays non-negative, updates the record's state byte and its linked records. The facts say the body starts in a gap that decodes as code, so it may be misread data.

name: mark_linked_records_when_counted
description: Decrements a per-record counter and, while it stays non-negative, sets the state byte on the record and on its linked records. It calls two other routines, and the facts say the body starts in a gap that decodes as code.

name: mark_chained_records_state
description: When a flag byte in the record is set, it writes a state value of 2 into the state bytes of the record's two linked records and then returns zero. The facts say the body starts in a gap that decodes as code.

name: test_overlap_window_set_flag
description: When the record's flag byte is non-zero, it compares two 16-bit positions against the record's fields and, if both axes fall within a window of sixteen before to thirty-two after, sets the flag byte to minus one and returns a non-zero value. Otherwise it returns the incoming register unchanged.

name: check_tile_collision_flag
description: Tests a tile-bit flag and a mode value, adjusts two position globals in sixteen-unit steps and returns a flag. When the byte at the pointer matches one of two special codes it sets a global and a second value. The facts list one instruction for this address, so the large body may be misdecoded data.

name: check_tile_collision_adjust
description: Checks a tile-bit flag and a mode value, calls other routines in several branches and adjusts two position globals in sixteen-unit steps, returning a flag. When the byte at the pointer matches one of two special codes it sets a global and a second value.

name: set_flag_on_special_code
description: Checks the byte at the pointer against two special codes and, on a match, sets a global to one and a second value to four. Otherwise it returns unchanged.

name: wrap_call_with_mode_flag
description: Sets a flag byte to one when a mode value is two, calls another routine and then clears the flag byte to zero.

name: wrap_calls_mode_flag
description: Sets a flag byte to four for mode three or to one for mode two, calls another routine and a second routine, then clears the flag byte to zero.

name: wrap_second_call_mode_flag
description: Applies the same mode-dependent flag setting as its neighbour, calling one other routine and a second routine before clearing the flag byte. The facts show only three instructions for this address, so the surrounding code may be shorter than the decompiled listing suggests.

name: test_tile_at_position_blocked
description: Converts two pixel-style coordinates into a tile index by dividing each by sixteen and combining them as a row-major index of width 200. It looks up the tile's attribute byte and returns a non-zero flag when its lowest bit is set, otherwise zero.

name: test_tile_attribute_blocked
description: Reads a tile index from the pointer, looks up its attribute byte and returns a non-zero flag when the lowest bit is set. Otherwise it returns the incoming register unchanged.

name: skip_empty_routine_body
description: The body is a bare return with no work, so calling it has no effect. Three unnamed routines call it.

name: flag_position_below_threshold
description: Returns a non-zero flag when a 16-bit position is below one hundred and otherwise returns the incoming register unchanged. The facts say the body starts in a gap that decodes as code, so it may be misread data.

name: program_blitter_tile_rows
description: Picks a source base, possibly after a bitmap test on the position, and computes a screen offset from the position in sixteen-unit steps. It then writes four blitter rows at a fixed plane stride, and the facts list the blitter address, modulo, control and size registers as touched.

name: check_neighbour_tiles_for_direction
description: For one character code it tests a tile bit in a bitmap and returns early when it is set. Otherwise it reads a tile attribute and, when a bit is set, combines four neighbour tests into a direction index before checking a table entry and a bitmap tile. It calls several routines for the neighbour tests.

name: store_longword_at_two_offsets
description: Writes one longword to two memory locations, each computed from a different base register plus a fixed offset.

name: stub_return_only_body
description: The decompiled body is a bare return, although the facts list four instructions with one call to an unnamed routine. Its behaviour is only partly recoverable from the evidence.

name: stub_return_only_tail
description: The decompiled body is a bare return, although the facts list four instructions with one call to an unnamed routine. Its behaviour is only partly recoverable from the evidence.

name: return_immediately_stub
description: The decompiled body is a bare return, and the facts list four instructions with one call to an unnamed routine. Its behaviour is only partly recoverable from the evidence.

name: return_immediately_shared_entry
description: The decompiled body is a bare return although the facts list 22 instructions. Four unnamed routines call it, so the real body may be misdecoded or the listing incomplete.

name: copy_tile_tables_to_buffer
description: Copies six words per pass from one source table and sixteen words per pass from a second table into a destination buffer, seven passes each. Destination writes step by a fixed row stride, so the two sets of source rows are interleaved in the output.

name: load_scaled_parameters_from_table
description: Looks up a pair of parameters in a table using a byte index, then stores them and products of them scaled by 22 and 21 into a large set of derived globals. It calls two other routines and works as a bulk parameter setup.

name: call_routine_pass_registers
description: Calls another routine and returns the incoming register values unchanged. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: cycle_four_state_slot_flags
description: Steps a four-state counter that wraps from zero to three. For each state it stores the incoming value in one of four slots and sets a matching flag. The facts list the DMA control register as touched, and the routine calls two other routines.

name: start_pending_audio_channel
description: Checks pending audio channel requests and, for the first one found, loads a sample pointer, length, period and volume from tables indexed by the sample number. It writes these to the audio channel registers and sets the matching DMA enable bit.

name: forward_call_keep_registers
description: Calls another routine and returns the incoming register values unchanged. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: start_audio_channel_by_index
description: Loads a sample pointer, length, period and volume for a sample index from the same tables, then writes them to the audio channel registers and sets a DMA enable bit. Which channel state is used depends on the pending flags.

name: tick_down_timer_counters
description: Decrements up to four timer counters and sets a related global to a fixed value each time one reaches zero. It returns its incoming register unchanged.

name: tick_timers_with_dma_update
description: Decrements the same four timer counters as its neighbour, setting related globals on expiry, and also writes the DMA control register. It calls two other routines.

name: run_memory_clear_sequence
description: Stores the text 'ello' into a global, clears and fills memory blocks in a fixed sequence and calls several routines, using a pointer table to choose the regions. When a flag is set it fills a block with a fixed longword pattern and then loops without end; the decompiled code is partly garbled.

name: configure_mode_parameters_by_state
description: Selects a setup block from a state value of one to six, storing parameter words, pointer values and mode settings for that state and calling other routines. Any other state value enters an endless loop. The facts list the colour, DMA and interrupt registers as touched.

name: set_single_mode_parameters
description: Sets a fixed group of parameter globals from constants and from two table values, stores a zero in a shared global and calls two other routines first.

name: copy_nine_records_from_table
description: Copies nine fixed-size records from a source table into globals, each record spaced by 32 bytes. It then sets a group of width and stride constants and calls another routine between two sets of constants.

name: return_no_op_shared
description: The body is a bare return with no work. Twenty-two unnamed routines call it, so it acts as a shared no-op.

name: add_constant_offset_to_register
description: Adds a fixed negative constant to the incoming register value and returns the result. The facts say the body starts in a gap that decodes as code, so it may be misdecoded data.

name: forward_call_return_only
description: Calls another routine and returns immediately with no other work. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: read_disk_sector_blocks
description: Writes the disk sync and disk length registers, then polls a disk status bit before copying bytes from a source buffer in blocks of 512 into memory. It steps through a table of source pointers and stops when its byte count runs out. The facts list only the colour register as touched, so the disk role rests on the register offsets in the code.

name: configure_disk_chip_registers
description: Writes control words to custom chip registers, including the DMA control register, sets and clears bits in a control byte, and runs a delay loop before returning. It calls three other routines.

name: wait_for_disk_status_clear
description: Sets one control bit, then repeats a delay loop and another call while a status bit stays set. It finally clears a word and another control bit, and it calls two other routines.

name: clear_word_and_control_bit
description: Clears a word at a pointer and clears bit 2 of a control byte. The facts report three instructions and an unreached gap, so the body may be incomplete.

name: reset_control_bits_and_wait
description: Sets one control bit, clears two others, runs a delay loop and then waits while a status bit stays set. It calls one other routine first.

name: read_disk_sector_blocks_alt
description: Repeats the disk read loop of its neighbour with the disk length register as the touched register in the facts. It writes the sync and length registers, waits on a status bit and copies 512-byte blocks through a table of pointers, and five unnamed routines call it.

name: read_disk_track_sectors
description: Waits for a disk sync pattern, then copies 512-byte sectors into memory from a table of track pointers, restarting the disk read registers after each track. It stops when its byte counter reaches zero and calls five other routines.

name: copy_disk_sectors_cia_port
description: Copies 512-byte disk blocks from a table of pointers into memory, advancing a state before each track. The facts list the CIA B port register as touched, and the copy stops when its counter reaches zero.

name: decode_mfm_sector_checksum
description: Scans for the disk sync pattern and decodes sector data by separating odd and even bits with an alternating-bit mask, XOR-accumulating a checksum as it goes. It stores each decoded sector pointer in a table indexed by sector number and stops when the checksum is non-zero or the sector count runs out.

name: combine_masked_longwords_shifted
description: Masks the incoming longword with the second word of a pair and ORs in the first word masked the same way and shifted left by one bit. It returns the combined value.

name: pass_stack_value_through
description: Returns the value taken from the stack without changing it. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: pass_stack_value_compare_entry
description: Returns the value taken from the stack unchanged, with the same body as its neighbour. Two unnamed routines reference its address in a comparison.

name: seek_disk_head_to_track
description: Steps a track counter up or down one track at a time until it reaches a target, toggling a control bit on the CIA port for each move. It first clears a status bit and waits while another status bit stays set. The facts list both CIA port registers as touched, and it calls seven other routines.

name: pulse_control_bit_with_delay
description: Sets bit 1 and then bit 0 of a control byte, clearing bit 0 in between, then runs a delay loop and returns its input unchanged.

name: reset_control_bit_with_delay
description: Clears bits 1 and 0 of a control byte, sets bit 0 again and runs a delay loop before returning its input unchanged. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: fill_buffer_alternating_pattern
description: Fills a block of 7,168 words starting at a pointer with an alternating-bit pattern and does nothing else. Five unnamed routines call it.

name: step_track_counter_to_target
description: Moves a counter one step up or down until it equals a target, then sets bit 2 of a control byte and clears it again when a low bit of the input is set. It calls one other routine, and the facts say the body starts in a gap that decodes as code.

name: skip_empty_port_stub
description: The body is a bare return, although the facts list touches of the CIA A port and the custom chip base register for its five unnamed callers. It is a stub, so its effect cannot be recovered from the body.

name: call_then_set_global_full
description: Calls another routine, then sets a global to a fixed full value and returns its input unchanged. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: search_name_table_for_match
description: Compares a text buffer held in a global against each 24-byte entry of a name table, returning when an entry matches. If none matches it sets a result code, and it may first call another routine to prepare the buffer. The facts reference a file name string.

name: scan_table_check_last_size
description: Walks a table of 24-byte entries until one has a zero first byte, then checks a size value derived from the last entry against a limit and sets a result code when it is exceeded. It calls another routine first when a flag is clear, and the facts say the body starts in a gap that decodes as code.

name: set_failure_result_code
description: Stores a fixed negative result code in a global and returns. The facts say the body starts in a gap that decodes as code, so it may be misdecoded data.

name: check_entry_size_limit
description: For a non-zero index, computes the address of a 24-byte table entry, adds two stored values and sets a failure code when the sum exceeds a fixed limit. It has no effect when the index is zero.

name: skip_empty_gap_routine
description: A bare return with no work, from a gap that decodes as code, so it is probably not a real routine.

name: copy_name_and_map_letters
description: Copies 16 bytes from a source string into a buffer, then maps each uppercase letter to a zero-based code, stopping at the zero terminator. The facts reference a file name string.

name: copy_table_rows_to_buffer
description: Copies bytes from a table region offset by a stored index into a destination pointer, decrementing a byte counter and advancing the source for each row. It calls five other routines, and the facts say the body starts in a gap that decodes as code.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler reached bad data and produced only a halt marker, so the body has no recoverable behaviour. The facts report 17 instructions, which the listing does not show.

name: stub_misdecoded_setup_data
description: The listing opens with a bad-data halt and then shows long setup sequences, but the facts report only one instruction for this address. Its behaviour cannot be reliably recovered from the evidence.

name: xor_byte_at_pointer
description: XORs a register value into a byte at a pointer and then ends in a bad-data halt. The facts report four instructions, so nothing beyond the XOR can be recovered.

key: switchblade ii (1991)(gremlin)[cr company][t +6 setrox]/Switchblade II (1991)(Gremlin)[cr Company][t +6 Setrox].adf:bootblock:0:000C
name: boot_setup_copper_list_display
description: Boot block code entered from the Kickstart strap. It calls several operating system library routines, including the exec I/O request routine, clears a block of memory and copies a small table. It then sets the copper list pointer, enables DMA and jumps to the copper, and the body ends in a bad-data halt.

key: switchblade ii (1991)(gremlin)[cr company][t +6 setrox]/Switchblade II (1991)(Gremlin)[cr Company][t +6 Setrox].adf:bootblock:0:01B0
name: start_disk_read_registers
description: Writes the disk sync word, the disk control word, the DMA control word and the disk length register, sets a bit on the CIA B port, then calls one other routine. The body ends in a bad-data halt.

key: switchblade ii (1991)(gremlin)[cr company][t +6 setrox]/Switchblade II (1991)(Gremlin)[cr Company][t +6 Setrox].adf:bootblock:0:0200
name: issue_disk_read_request
description: Fills in an I/O request block with a read length, a buffer pointer and a fixed disk offset, then calls an operating system library routine through the exec base to carry it out. It sets the command field again afterwards.

key: Switchblade II (1991)(Gremlin)[cr Company][t +6 Setrox].adf boot-block load +$97400 to $050000 (5632 bytes):0:0116
name: store_shifted_longword_flag
description: Reads a longword just before a base pointer, stores a two-byte value at a second pointer and returns the longword shifted right by one with its top bit set. The facts list two calls that the listing does not show.

key: Switchblade II (1991)(Gremlin)[cr Company][t +6 Setrox].adf boot-block load +$97400 to $050000 (5632 bytes):0:0130
name: shift_bits_refilling_from_source
description: Shifts a bit buffer right one bit per pass for a count held in a register, calling another routine to refill the buffer when it runs out. The facts list two unnamed calls.

name: initialise_copper_display_loop
description: The first code of this unit: a long setup sequence that writes many globals, clears memory, copies tables into buffers, sets the copper list pointer and enables DMA, then runs a loop over text and table data. The listing is cut off partway, so the full flow is only partly recoverable.

name: update_timer_and_reload_display
description: Counts a frame timer down and, when it expires, clears a block of memory, reloads display tables from source data and sets the copper list pointers. It then runs a loop over text-driven graphics. The listing is cut off partway, so the full sequence is only partly recoverable.

name: handle_name_entry_key
description: Handles one key code for a name entry: one specific code deletes the last character by replacing it with a space, and other codes are stored into an eight-character buffer as the index advances. Codes outside the handled range leave the buffer unchanged. The facts list a dot-only text reference.

name: jump_through_fixed_vector
description: Calls a fixed address through a code pointer and returns. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: draw_text_string_glyphs
description: Draws a zero-terminated text string into display memory by looking up each character's glyph in a font table and copying its six rows at a fixed stride. Spaces advance the cursor by eight, digits and letters map to glyph indices, and the routine calls another routine when it reaches the end marker.

name: set_sprite_six_seven_pointers
description: Writes pattern values to the sprite 6 and sprite 7 pointer registers, calling two other routines when a flag is zero. It then writes fixed constants and derives a status flag from bits of a register value.

name: draw_two_digit_number_text
description: Converts a value into two digit characters by adding a character offset, then draws them as text through the same glyph loop as its neighbour. It calls one other routine first.

name: show_completion_screen_setup
description: Runs when a state value equals minus one. In one branch it reloads display tables, sets the copper list pointers and enables DMA, and it references the text '1 COMPLETE', which suggests a completion screen. The listing is cut off partway, so the full sequence is only partly recoverable.

name: tally_counter_and_draw_score
description: Decrements one of three counters per call in a fixed priority order and draws the five-digit value from a digit buffer beside a fixed label through the glyph text loop. It returns when all three counters are zero.

name: tally_secondary_counter_draw
description: Decrements one of two counters, falling back to the second when the first is zero, and draws a five-digit value through the glyph text loop. It returns when both counters are zero.

name: tally_last_counter_draw
description: Decrements a single counter when it is non-zero and draws the five-digit value beside a label through the glyph text loop. The text reference is a string of six nines.

name: draw_fixed_label_text
description: Points at a fixed text string, calls one other routine and then draws the string through the glyph text loop.

name: stub_large_body_bare_return
description: The decompiled listing is only a bare return, although the facts report 448 instructions, a text reference, three callers and six unnamed calls. The real behaviour cannot be recovered from the evidence.

name: update_sprite_record_from_table
description: Writes fixed control words into a sprite-style record, then sets its position and size from a table indexed by a state value. It calls one other routine and advances a frame index that wraps to zero at a sentinel entry.

name: update_sprite_record_from_index
description: Writes control words into a sprite-style record for the current entry, sets its position from a table, then advances a frame index that wraps to zero at a sentinel. It is nearly the same as its neighbour without the separate setup of the first record.

name: clear_bitplane_block_rows
description: When a flag is set, clears a rectangular area of display memory by writing zeros across thirty rows and eight columns, with each cell cleared in five plane-spaced locations. Otherwise it returns. It calls an empty routine.

name: format_two_digit_value_pointer
description: Converts a value into two digit characters, sets a pointer to the digit buffer and calls two other routines around the conversion. The pointer is cleared after use when it is non-zero.

name: call_and_store_pointer_result
description: When a stored pointer is non-zero, calls one other routine and stores the value it returns back into the pointer. It has no effect otherwise.

name: draw_glyph_character_planes
description: Draws one character from a text pointer into five bitplanes of display memory using a glyph table with per-character offsets. Spaces only advance the cursor, commas and question marks map to fixed glyph slots, and digits and letters map to their own glyph indices. The text and display pointers advance after each character.

name: find_region_containing_point
description: When a bitmap bit at the current position is set, searches a table of four-word rectangles for one that contains the current point, using sentinel values to skip groups. It then calls several routines to act on the region it found and returns a value.

name: draw_frame_tile_columns
description: Advances a frame index and, depending on which of four cases it matches, picks a source table and copies seven-row tile columns into display memory at a fixed stride. It calls two other routines in its branches.

name: copy_tile_columns_downward
description: Copies seven-row tile columns from a source table into display memory for each index from a counter down to zero, using the same row stride as its neighbour. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: stub_no_recoverable_body
description: The decompiled body is only removal warnings and a truncation marker, so no code is shown. The facts list a DMA control register write, a text reference and calls to two empty routines and three unnamed routines, but the behaviour cannot be recovered from the evidence.

name: clear_bitmap_cells_in_rectangles
description: Walks a list of four-word rectangles up to a sentinel and clears the bitmap bit for every cell inside each rectangle, using a row-major index of width 200.

name: stub_misdecoded_state_machine
description: The listing shows a long state machine over eight table entries with several calls, but the facts report only two instructions for this address, so the body is probably misdecoded. Its purpose cannot be reliably recovered.

name: stub_truncated_state_machine
description: The listing is a long state machine over eight table entries and is cut off partway, while the facts report six instructions for this address. The behaviour cannot be reliably recovered from the evidence.

name: stub_short_state_machine_variant
description: A variant of the same eight-entry state machine as its neighbours, shown truncated in the listing. The facts report eight instructions and two callers, so its behaviour cannot be reliably recovered from the evidence.

name: update_eight_entry_state_machine
description: Runs an eight-entry state update over table records: it calls a set of routines, sets record fields from the state and a position value, and advances the state index with wrap-around. The listing is cut off partway, so the full sequence is only partly recoverable.

name: copy_longword_relative_offset
description: Copies a longword from a location four bytes before a base pointer plus an offset to the location at the base pointer plus the same offset. The facts report 158 instructions, far more than the single copy shown, so the listing may be incomplete.

name: copy_relative_cells_to_buffer
description: Copies a longword and a byte between buffers at offsets from three pointers, and writes a value from a pointer table entry. The facts list three calls that the listing does not show.

name: move_object_deactivate_offscreen
description: When an object record is active, moves its horizontal position by nine units in the direction of a flag. If the position leaves a window around a global reference it deactivates the record and calls two other routines, otherwise it stays active.

name: spawn_paired_child_records
description: When a record is inactive, allocates a new record through another routine, initialises it with a position offset and links a second record to it with a different offset and attributes. It calls several routines and returns once both records are set.

name: animate_and_move_active_object
description: When an object record is active, cycles its frame counter through four frames and picks the image byte from a table depending on a flag. It moves the horizontal position by nine units and deactivates the record, calling two other routines, when the position leaves the window.

name: spawn_single_object_record
description: When a record is inactive, allocates a new object record through another routine and initialises its position and frame attributes. It writes a second position set when a flag is set and calls other routines along the way, as the single-record form of its neighbour's spawn logic.

name: dispatch_record_handler_by_type
description: Loads the record in a fixed slot and, when the slot is not empty, calls a handler chosen from a table by the record's type byte. The facts list a call to an empty stub.

name: loop_forever_trap
description: Loops forever with no body, so the routine never returns. Six unnamed routines call it, which suggests a fatal or waiting loop.

name: advance_timed_record_dispatch
description: Decrements a delay counter in a record and, when it reaches zero, advances an index through a table with wrap-around. It spawns a record from a table entry and calls a handler chosen from a second table, and it makes five calls to unnamed routines in total.

name: reset_countdown_when_idle
description: When two state bytes are zero, sets a countdown to a fixed value less six, clamps it at zero and increments it, then clears two flags. It returns early when a flag is set.

name: copy_five_row_pairs
description: Copies five rows of two table bytes into display memory, storing each pair at two fixed offsets from a row base that a stored index selects.

name: accumulate_cell_threshold_counts
description: Loops over fifteen rows of thirty packed cells, comparing each cell's nibbles with the row index and bumping counter bytes when a nibble is below it. Each row also increments a set of counters and makes two calls to unnamed routines.

name: decay_cell_nibbles_per_row
description: Over fifteen passes it makes two calls to unnamed routines, then decrements each non-zero nibble of thirty packed cells and each non-zero entry of a sixteen-entry counter table. When a flag is set it first fills the counter table with ascending indices.

name: boot_copy_low_memory_setup
description: A boot-style sequence that copies a block of words from a fixed source into low memory, selects a copper list through an operating system call and runs a setup sequence similar to the boot block's. It contains bad-data halts on failed checks.

name: call_routine_and_return_regs
description: Calls another routine and returns the register pair unchanged. The facts list two callers.

name: decode_markers_bounded_lz_stream
description: Scans for a start marker and an end marker in the data, then reads the packed stream backwards from the end. It decodes bits into back-reference lengths and offsets, copies output bytes backwards and calls one other routine for bit refills.

name: shift_bit_buffer_with_refill
description: Shifts a bit buffer one bit per pass for a count held in a register, loading a new byte when the buffer empties and rotating the pair of carry registers. It is the bit extraction step of the decoder.

name: configure_cia_ports_and_interrupts
description: Writes control values to the CIA A and CIA B registers, sets an interrupt enable value and stores a vector in a global, then calls one other routine. The facts list the CIA A port, interrupt enable and interrupt request registers as touched.

name: save_registers_and_handle_interrupt
description: Saves the full register set to fixed low-memory slots, then checks a CIA control bit and, when it is set, calls one routine and sets a bit in a device register block. It returns the saved register pair.

name: set_bit6_and_flag_register
description: Calls one other routine, sets bit 6 of a byte at one register block offset, writes 1 to another offset, sets a global to a fixed value and returns the saved register pair.

name: clear_bit6_of_register_block
description: Clears bit 6 of a byte at a fixed offset from the base register and then stores 8 in a global. The facts record an INTREQ touch, which fits acknowledging an interrupt request bit.

name: advance_counter_state_machine
description: Steps a global value through range checks: depending on the range it returns, adds or subtracts fixed increments, or resets the value, calls another routine and retries the same branch.

name: run_stage_dependent_draw_loop
description: Returns at once when the stage value is zero. For higher stages it picks a base offset from the stage and writes three words per pass in a five-pass loop with a fixed stride; for lower stages it calls another routine four times and advances the stage.

name: setup_blitter_copy_rows
description: Computes a start offset from the stage value and an input register, adjusts it by constants and writes the blitter masks, modulo, pointer, control and size registers. It then runs a five-pass loop that steps the pointers by a fixed stride.

name: repeat_routine_and_advance_global
description: Calls another routine and advances a global counter by two on each pass, repeating one more time than the count held in a register.

name: stub_no_decompiled_body
description: The decompiler produced no body for this routine, and the facts report five instructions reached through an absolute address. Its behaviour cannot be determined from the evidence.

name: stub_calls_one_routine
description: The decompiler produced no body for this eight-instruction routine, which calls one unnamed routine. Its behaviour cannot be determined from the evidence.

name: copy_indexed_table_rows
description: Increments a global, branches on its value to pick one of four table bases and calls a routine in each case. It then copies pairs of bytes from the lookup table into a destination at a fixed row stride; the bundle reports only one instruction for this address, so the body may be misdecoded data.

name: decode_mouse_port_direction
description: Reads the mouse port movement register and reduces its bit patterns to a small direction state held in a global.

name: split_value_into_decimal_digits
description: Converts a value to digits by repeatedly subtracting entries from a zero-terminated table of place values and storing each count as one byte. It is a number-to-digits conversion.

name: test_position_against_bounds_storing
description: Tests a value against ranges built from two words at a pointer, each widened by 100 and a fixed offset. It returns zero when the value falls inside a range and a non-zero flag otherwise, and it also stores several values through the stack and the second pointer register.

name: test_position_in_bounds_box
description: Tests a value against ranges built from two words at a pointer, each widened by 100 and a fixed offset. It returns zero on a hit and a non-zero flag otherwise, without the stack stores of its neighbour.

name: repeat_routine_until_both_zero
description: Calls another routine repeatedly and loops while either of its two returned values stays non-zero, stopping once both are zero.

name: reset_state_and_clear_block
description: Decrements a state value and, through several branches, calls other routines, stores a lookup record and clears a block of words in a loop. The facts list the COLOR00 colour register as touched, and the bundle cuts the decompiled body off partway, so the full sequence cannot be confirmed.

name: clear_then_enable_dma_interrupts
description: Writes constants to the DMA and interrupt control registers, starting with a DMA set mask and a clear-all mask for the interrupt enables. It calls another routine between the writes and then writes further enable masks.

name: enable_dma_and_interrupt_bits
description: Writes a DMA set mask to the DMA control register and a clear-all mask to the interrupt enable register. It calls two routines around a final set mask for the interrupt enables.

name: return_without_action
description: The body is a single return with no work, so calling it has no effect.

name: move_position_by_key_code
description: Adjusts two 16-bit values in a table entry selected by the key code. Each of four comparisons against a key code adds or subtracts one from one of the values, so it looks like a keyboard direction update.

name: repack_value_nibbles
description: Divides the value by 200 and folds the quotient into the high nibble, then transforms the low nibble and combines the two. The result is written back to the same global.

name: reset_sprite_pointers_if_flagged
description: When a flag bit is set, it writes a fixed constant eight times, matching the eight sprite pointer registers listed in the facts, then calls another routine and sets a global. Otherwise it only sets a global to a fixed value.

name: summarise_timed_out_routine
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code is available. The facts show 62 instructions that touch the COLOR00 colour register and the DMACON DMA control register, a file path string, and a series of small move and OR routines.

name: call_routine_over_nested_grid
description: Runs a nested loop of 26 outer passes and 28 inner passes, calling another routine once per inner pass. The loop itself does no other work in this code.

name: call_routine_twenty_eight_times
description: Calls another routine 28 times in a row using a byte counter. The facts say the start of this body lies in a gap that decodes as code, so it may be misread data.

name: call_routine_if_value_high
description: Compares a global against a threshold and, when it is at or above it, calls another routine 26 times. Otherwise it returns without work.

name: call_routine_twenty_six_times
description: Calls another routine 26 times in a row using a byte counter and does nothing else.

name: call_routine_then_return
description: Calls another routine and then performs a self-assignment to a global, which has no effect, before returning. Four unnamed routines call it.

name: place_template_object_in_grid
description: Computes a grid cell from two register values and tests bit flags in a bitmap and a byte map. It returns if the cell is blocked or already marked; otherwise it marks the cell, calls another routine and fills a 30-byte record with coordinates scaled by 16 plus offsets from a template table.

name: fill_object_record_from_template
description: Marks a map byte as occupied, calls another routine and then fills an object record from a template picked by a table lookup. Coordinates are scaled by 16 with offsets, and 30 bytes of template data are copied into the record.

name: initialise_tables_and_records
description: Sets a run of globals to zero and a few constants, fills two record tables with minus-one values and clears a bit in a byte region. It calls several routines and runs a five-pass loop that writes two constants and calls a routine each pass, so it is setup code whose wider purpose is not recoverable from this body.

name: release_list_head_node
description: Returns when the list head is a sentinel. Otherwise it takes the first node, decrements the stored count, and either resets the node's fields when the count reaches minus one or links the node back into the list with its status byte set.
